ost.outcome: A user of rn sees what they asked for work on the real thing early in a run, and grows it from there.

opportunities.opportunity: I see what I asked for work on the real thing early.
opportunities.by: #86: 6,079 lines before the first real check in #85

opportunities.opportunity: I pick what to meet first, without spelling out every detail.
What I first touch already holds the quality its kind needs.
It works in a large existing app, aimed at what I'm after now.

solution.solution: Rebuild rn as prompts and work scripts on one steering file per run, its opportunity solution tree for the moment's goal, making the least solution as one walking skeleton.
solution.why: It puts something that runs in the user's hands before most is made, and keeps no tree of the whole product to maintain.

assumption.assumption: Given the opportunities on the ost, the pruner keeps every named one, the user can pick, and the run reaches a real check before most deliverables are made.
assumption.test: Run rn from this branch on #62 up to the first real check; count what was made by then.
assumption.result: Failed on #62 (2026-11-26): the hearing and the pick held, and every named need stayed, but after 1h20m the run had made 7 of 10 deliverables, 834 lines, with nothing the user could try, as each put-up pushed through the repository's checks, which pulled in tests, coverage, check.sh, and trace.py before the hook that runs it; and its messages spoke of rn's insides while roles worked.

opportunities.opportunity: From there, I grow it one addition at a time, and keep each thing I asked for.
A mend I ask for lands at once.
An addition keeps the quality of what's there.
No need I named is dropped without my say.
At the end, I decide what happens to what I didn't pick.

decisions.decision: Talk with the user in Japanese and write each deliverable in English, as the user reads Japanese and the repository is in English.
Pile up the vital few and cut the trivial many thoroughly, as rn's center.
Make the least solution as one walking skeleton and check its riskiest assumption on the real thing first, so the run knows it reaches the goal before it builds much.
Make the opportunity solution tree for one run, so rn aims at the moment's goal, in a large existing app too.
Put each opportunity that people name on the tree for the user to pick, as the user decides what's dropped, not a role.
Show the opportunities in the user's words, numbered, with rn's pick and its grounds, so the user judges only which one brings the outcome closest.
Have the user give feedback as one who uses it, and rn settle how it's made and explain the solution only when asked, so the user's time goes to what only they can judge.
Make the least, and use the best practices in full on what's made, so less made costs no quality.
Propose at the run's end what to do with each unpicked opportunity, so the user decides what stays.
Keep the steering in one file with one writer to each part, so no part has two writers.
Make a unit case for each class that an interface's contract treats apart, with C0 and C1 at 100%, so each requirement has its case and no line lacks a requirement.
Have the user run the walking skeleton as the E2E check, so what works is judged by one who uses it.

Add a test above the unit level only for a fault that the user's run found and that should have been caught before it, or for an operation that can't be undone, so tests grow from evidence, not from what the design draws.
Make a test design or a test implementation only when a key result needs what the user's run can't show, such as a measure over many runs, so no test machinery is built ahead of need.
Make a deliverable in Rounds only when it's first made or remade, against every condition of its best practice, so its first quality is built in before the user touches it.

Make a change that adds what the people can do in Rounds for the added part alone, with the evaluator judging only the conditions it touches, as only one who tries it as the people would sees whether it serves them.

Have the fixer make a change that brings back what was promised, such as a fault or the user's mend, at once, checking it by the kind's best practice and the unit tests itself, so a mend waits for no Round.
Call an opportunity 「できるようにしたいこと」 to rn's users, as they don't know the opportunity solution tree.
Work one step at a time, in order, and remove the old before making the new, so the branch never holds two ways at once.
Keep tests green and push on each commit, so each step stands on checked work.
Do the work alone, with no subagents, so one judgment keeps documents, scripts, and prompts in step.
Give work outside #86's purpose its own issue, herdr worktree, and pull request, so it reaches main without waiting.
Speak to the user in plain words, never in rn's or the plan's own terms, so the user follows without learning them.
Leave issue #86 as it was asked, as it's the request that started the work.
Keep /rn:on, /rn:up, /rn:dn, /rn:ty, and /rn:gm, so the user starts, stops, picks up, approves, and asks for a mend each by its own command.
Check the pull request whole before the merge is proposed, as any careful team does.
Leave the pull request's CI to the user, who sees it on the pull request before they merge, as waiting for it brings nothing in the user's hands earlier.
Have /rn:up go on with the run of the branch the user is on, and ask which only elsewhere, so the user names the run by where they type.
Write each prompt's steps by their purpose and intent, checked against every condition of the prompt best practice, so the AI judges a case the steps don't name.

Write each message to the user in one shape, with no heading such as 「いま：」: first one sentence of what was done, with how far the run is to the try as (2/4) where it counts, then what the user does now, either one question with numbered options, each with a line on what it leads to and the recommended one marked, or the command to try, and nothing after it. List once, when making starts, what is made before the try. Tell nothing of rn's insides, such as a test or a fix, and end a turn on such an event with an empty reply, so the user sees how far the run has come and gives feedback at once, as Spec Kit and AI-DLC report progress against the plan shown first.
Call a run off on the user's words, such as 中止して, once they confirm what goes, removing its worktree, branch, and pull request, as rn 0.11.0 did, and keep /rn:dn for a stop for now.

Have the orchestrator hear from the user whom the run is for and what for, one question at a time, and hand the hearing to a pruner only once it is whole, as rn 0.11.0 did, since a pruner can't talk with the user and a request needs no issue.
Show the pick as the question, then each need numbered in the user's words alone, with no restated outcome and no means, the recommended one marked with why in one sentence.

Before choosing how to meet the picked need, look for what already meets it, such as Claude Code's own features, a tool its people have, or a part of the repository, reading public documents too, and make only what it lacks, as #62 found Claude Code's built-in auto-continue only after 8 of 10 deliverables.

Send a change to a part that others share outside what the run delivers, such as the repository's checks, out of the run, asking the user once whether to give it its own issue, so the run holds only its purpose.

Write each prompt in domain/ in three sections, Role, what the role is expected to achieve, Steps, each step's purpose and intent with only the plugin's own rules, and Output, what it hands back, as the entries hold the form that Claude Code fixes, so each line changes what the AI does.
Read each rewritten prompt through with the user, one at a time, the orchestrator's first, as the user judges whether its length fits rn as they use and designed it.

steps.settles: the product vision's Concept, as agreed
the README: what rn promises its users, and the walkthrough of the first mode
the steering's form, so the run's aim and standing have one shape from now on
the architecture of the least rn, by the architecture best practice, from the README; then every part it doesn't hold is removed
the scripts, by TDD at their least, each existing part taken only where the architecture gives it a role
the prompts, by the prompt best practice, taking the best of the existing ones
a desk trace of the whole run in order, from the issue to the walking skeleton in the user's hands
the prompt best practice and its template, in Role, Steps, and Output
the README and the architecture, for messages in one shape and the findings of #62
the prompts, rewritten in Role, Steps, and Output with the fixes of the findings of #62, read through with the user one at a time
the user's E2E run of rn from this branch on #62, up to the first real check, as the solution's assumption test
